newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 24.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 24.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Thursday:
* Investors will continue to be on the defensive awaiting more corporate earnings result for the first half of the year and until concerns on the currency market ebb further, traders said.

* "The market seems plagued by anxiety over the long wait for second quarter corporate results to come out...investors are still wary of resuming trading due to uncertainties on how the recent peso depreciation will affect listed firms," BPI Securities Corp said in its daily outlook.
* On Wednesday, the Philippine composite index closed lower by 20.36 points at 2,636.37 points.
* The Dow Jones on Wednesday ended 26.71 points higher at 8,088.36. PLDT's ADR closed up $0/15 at $32 1/2.
* The Philippine peso ended lower at 28.5 to a dollar vs the previous close of 28.15.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was steady at 25.0625 percent.

* The Philippine National Bank said it is likely to meet its 2.1 billion peso net income forecast this year despite missing its target in the first six months. PNB posted a net profit of 955 million pesos in the first half of the year compared with 701 million a year ago.

* The Philippine central bank, tightening the noose for those trying to toy with the currency, said it was limiting the amount of dollars onshore banks could hold and effectively barred them from selling dollars offshore in the non-deliverable forward (NDF) market, a derivatives market based in Singapore.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange said it will ask 23 listed firms to expand their stockholders' base to more than 500.

* Philippine President Fidel Ramos has approved the privatisation of PNOC-Energy Development Corp in the second half of the year, Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said. PNOC-EDC is the geothermal arm of PNOC.

* A unit of Ayala Land Inc, Ayala International Properties Pte Ltd said it had joined a consortium to buy the Forum, a retail and office building complex along Orchard Road in Singapore for S$359 million.
* Newspaper BusinessWorld said the peso's fall is likely to reduce the country's trade deficit to 10 billion pesos.

* Manila Bulletin said the Securities and Exchange Commission has finally decided to revoke permanently the license of the Manila International Futures Exchange as a venue for the trading of currency and commodities future contracts in the country.
